recipes.name: Killer Bacon-Cheese Dogs
ingredients_raw: 0.5 cup barbeque sauce, or amount to taste

steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat. Lightly oil grate, and set 4 inches from the heat.
Place the bacon in a large, deep skillet. Cook over medium-high heat until evenly brown. Drain on paper towels.
Place hot dogs on grill; cook until browned, 5 to 8 minutes, turning once, or until done to suit your taste.
To assemble sandwiches, place a slice of cheese and bacon on each roll. Add a hot dog, top each with 1 tablespoon barbeque sauce, or desired amount, and red onion.

raw_recipe.headline: Killer Bacon-Cheese Dogs
raw_recipe.description: Give your family's next grilled hot dog roast a little zip by making bacon-cheese dogs. Simply layer hot dog buns with Swiss cheese and bacon slices, top each with a dog, barbeque sauce, and diced red onion, and have a feast!

video.description: Amp up your hot dogs with bacon and cheese! Your favorite flavors are the perfect addition to the classic hot dog.

review.reviewBody: I like your recipe i do this instead took hotdogs sliced 3/4 way through an stuffed with cheese an then wrapped with the bacon an used toothpicks to hold bacon in place. Then griled cheese side down at first when cheese starts to melt turn hot dogs an finish cooking. We have been doing this for years, family an friends love them.

Have made a similar recipe for yours: Slice dogs lenghtwise (not all the way through) place cheese of choice in dog, wrap partially cooked bacon strip around dog, secure bacon with toothpicks and either broil or grill til done. We called them "Swanky Frankies". I and the kids loved them!

A fun weekend food. It was too cold to grill today so I assembled these slightly different. I just tossed the bacon and onion in a fry pan for a few minutes, with the hot dogs. I assembled the buns, cheese, hotdogs, onion bacon and bbq sauce then I broiled them for just about 2-3 minutes on high with an extra 1/2 slice of cheese on top. The kids and hubby loved them and polished them off! Frying up the onion with the bacon really helped take the bite off so the kids could enjoy it too. The bbq sauce was something fun and out of the ordinary than ketchup. Even in on cold winter days you can still enjoy this food if you just prepare it with a little imagination.

We’ve had hot dogs in the freezer for some time now and I wanted to use them up, so I thought we’d give this recipe a try. I wrapped the hotdog with the bacon and secured it with toothpicks. Hubs grilled them until the bacon was crisp all around. We tried a couple of versions to see which we liked best. I had both Swiss cheese as well as pepperjack, and I put out both barbeque sauce and mustard, and of course the chopped red onion. I think both Hubs and I preferred the pepperjack with mustard over the Swiss with barbeque sauce. All in all, for us this was just a hotdog. I’m not sure I liked it any better than a plain old hotdog slathered with mustard, but it was fun to try something new.

My husband is NOT a hotdog eater! But when I served this to him, he said this is the MAN version of a hotdog. I did add 2 strips of bacon to each dog and I also put the Swiss cheese on the bread and threw it into the toaster oven until the cheese was bubbly, it was great!
The right way to make these is to slice the hotdog 3/4 deep and stuff with cheese then wrap with bacon, secure with toothpicks and either grill or cook under the broiler

I should preface this review w/a disclaimer: I'm a hot dog purist. I prefer hot dogs roasted over a campfire, on a cheap bun, w/mustard and onions. For some reason, this recipe caught my eye and I've been craving it since I added it to my recipe box. We made them tonight and they were just as delicious as I'd anticipated, though I did opt to sub yellow mustard for BBQ sauce, cause I'm just not a BBQ fan and knew it would really throw off the taste for me. Other than, that, good stuff! I'm lazy, so I nuked 2 slices of Oscar Meyer Center Cut bacon for a couple of minutes to make the process even easier. While this won't become THE way of eating hot dogs for me (still the fire, yellow mustard, onions...), I WILL make these whenever we have some swiss to use. THANKS, drink spiller (BTW-have you tried a sippy cup?)!
5 stars for flavor. If you're going to need a lot of bacon though, a lot better in a 400 oven for 10-15 minutes than cooking in a pan. Easier and the bacon stays flat. Less greasy too.
Perfect for summer! I will use this recipe while camping over an open fire. Perfect blend I also used scallions and had a great taste. Quick and Easy!

My family just discovered hotdogs cooked this way about a year ago, but we will never eat another "regular" hotdog again. Only difference is I wrap the bacon around the hotdog and secure it at each end with a toothpick. Once the bacon is done the hotdog is done. You can then remove the toothpick because the bacon holds the wrapped shape once it is done. YUM!!!

I made exactly as written except cooked them in the broiler oven - split the dogs lengthwise when almost done and put the cheese & bacon slice in the dog. I then put them under the broiler until cheese melted. Very good!
I usually only ever allow ketchup and mustard on my hot dogs, but the barbecue sauce was a nice pace change. Bacon, cheese, onions - what's not to love about this?!
Family really liked these, however I think I will wrap the bacon around the hot dog next time.
Family and I loved this recipe!
Super good
Delicious! My kiddo devoured this! You really can't go wrong with bacon on a grilled dog :) Loved the addition of barbeque sauce too!
My husband loves these, in capital letters. I hate hot dogs, but this makes them palatable.
yum!
These were awesome! We followed the recipe exactly. I used Sweet Baby Ray's BBQ sauce and it turned out awesome. I would make again!
Simple and tasty!
